Shailendra Kr. Tiwari, Spl.P.P.

03/10.01.2025 Both these Bail Applications arise out of same police case.
Accordingly, both these Bail Applications are being disposed of by a common order.
Heard the parties.

The petitioners have been made accused in connection with Cyber Crime No.52 of 2024, arising out of Deoghar (Cyber) P.S. Case No.97 of 2023, for the offences registered under Sections 419 /420/
467/ 468/ 471/ 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 66(B), 66(C), 66(D) and 84(C) of the I.T. Act, pending in the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum- Special Judge, Cyber Crime, Deoghar.

sentences.text: 1 Bail Application of the petitioner Siraj Ansari was earlier rejected by this Court vide B.A. No.1751 of 2024 by order dated 07.05.2024 while Bail Application of the petitioner Sandip Kumar Yadav was earlier rejected by this Court vide B.A. No.1820 of 2024 by order dated 07.05.2024.
Both these petitioners were apprehended by Cyber Police, Deoghar on the allegation that they had assembled in the village- Basbutia for committing cyber-crime.
On search, mobile phones and other e-gadgets were recovered from their possession.
During the course of investigation, it transpired that victims had claimed that mobile phones so recovered from their possession was used in cheating them.
It was submitted that petitioners are remained in custody for more than one year.
It was further submitted that similarly situated co-accused Krishna Kumar Das whose case stands on similar footing, has been granted bail by this Court vide B.A. No.9206 of 2024.
Learned Spl.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail.
Considering the submissions made above, I am inclined to release the petitioners, on bail.

Accordingly, the petitioners, named above, are directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum- Special Judge, Cyber Crime, Deoghar, in connection with Cyber Crime No.52 of 2024, arising out of Deoghar (Cyber) P.S. Case No.97 of 2023.
